title: Band personnel: Willie Long, Scott Bagby and turnover
summary: Dixon's main instrument was tuba; Scott Bagby played piano by ear; Floyd's band had little turnover while Albert was there.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I wondered about that band. A whole lot of things, you know. He seemed to have a quite unusual style. I never heard anybody else play trombone quite like Charlie Dixon.

Well, Charlie Dixon wasn't on the trombone play. His main instrument was the tuba. And that got along on the trombone. And both of them, he'd get a tremendous tone. Willie Long also was a fairly good reader. And so was Benny. Benny wasn't a real fast reader, but they were what we call spellers. And you get together with these guys that can read little and you knowing how it should go when you play it for them and they'd get it on you. Well, it wouldn't take long to run these arrangements down and get them. Well, then they had pretty good ears. Good ears. For instance, this fellow, Scott Bagby. Scott Bagby played a tremendous piano. Up until today, I don't believe Scott Bagby would know one note from the other. But he would put a sheet of music in front of him and it's remarkable. When the notes went up, he went up. When he came down, he finally was getting the perfect harmony. He still lived in his way up in the seventies. He's a very active man. He plays church music now. Where does he live? He lives in San Antonio.
Well, do you know where he got his style? I was especially curious because of what Gunther Schiller had to say in his book.

I think, I'm not passing any criticism. I think there's a little misinformation there. Scott Bagby is just one of these natural musicians. And his playing was just a gift to him. And after he played the clarinet and he got into Troy's band, and by doubling their playing was just one of their first-minded families. Men would come and go. No not too many in that band. My band had a lot of changes but not Troy's band. They only changed, well after yes after I left he started to change a lot of musicians to try to keep the remnants going. But when I was there it was almost a family affair because we all worked together with each other. And Scott Bagley was the only one that I could remember that dropped out and got a replacement with Herschel Evans. Because Fred Murphy didn't want to leave Dallas, Texas I tried to get Fred to join the band. Fred he didn't want to, he played a few days with us until we could get a replacement.
